1. Introduction

The Timesheet module in Quotelan is designed to record the time spent by employees on different tasks, projects, or activities. It helps organizations track labor hours, billable and non-billable hours, leave, overtime (OT), double time (DT), triple time (TT), and payroll processes. Timesheet module is also used to track punch-in/punch-out (in and out entry) of every employee to the company. Timesheets can be created, modified, approved, rejected, reset, copied, and exported based on user permissions.

2. Timesheet Module - Functional Architecture & Workflow

Weekly Timesheet Structure Based on your company policy, you can initially decide the start day of the week. By default, Quoteplan shows Monday however this company setting can be changed before you start the timesheet module.

Create and Save Timesheet :

In this functionality, a user can create and save their timesheet for a selected week. Steps Click on the Menu. Select Time Tracking. Click on Create Timesheet. Select the required week using the Calendar Picker (Sunday to Saturday). By default Quoteplan shows current week Verify the selected week range and Today’s date displayed on the top-right corner. user can select 1 year prior today’s date or user can fill timesheet for 2 weeks in advance. User can fill timesheet for PTO labor code 6 months in advance. For any other labor code, system will generate message You can only create and submit PTO 6 months in advance. Select a Project from the Project dropdown. User can see only specific projects for which user is assigned. User can select only labor codes assigned for that user for that project. Also user can select assigned tasks for that project. User-labor, user-task, task-labor permissions are assigned in project module - project settings. Select a Task from the Task dropdown. (if task is enabled for your timesheet) Select Labor from the Labor dropdown. Select Type from the dropdown (REG / OT / DT / TT).

The system automatically performs both row-level and timesheet-level calculations, including:

Regular Hours Overtime Double Time Triple Time Total Time (not to exceed > 24 hrs per day) Billable Hours Non-Billable Hours PTO Hours (PTO labor code) Holiday Hours (Holiday labor code) Total Hours Hours Worked (=Total hrs - non payable) Non-Payable Hours (for Lunch and FMEA labor types only) Supplemental bonus (comes from numeric value written in comment section in timesheet. Eg: $100 for customer support - this will show 100 in supplemental bonus ) All calculations are dynamically recalculated whenever hours or configuration values change.

4. Row Management Behavior

After creating or opening a timesheet, users can add, edit, or delete rows. Row deletion is allowed before emailing the timesheet. After a row is deleted, all dependent calculated fields (such as Billable and Non-Billable hours) are recalculated automatically. When the Project field is changed in a row, all dependent fields (Labor, Task, Type, Hours, and Billable flag) are reset to avoid invalid data mapping. If a row contains zero hours, the system triggers a confirmation alert before saving. The Hours field accepts numeric values only

5. Viewing and Modifying Existing Timesheets

To modify an existing timesheet, the user accesses it through the View / Modify section. The user can change the timesheet anytime as long as the row is not locked. Once the timesheet is emailed, then the row becomes locked to prevent accidental changes. Users must explicitly unlock the timesheet using the Lock icon if user has permission If permission validation fails, the timesheet remains in read-only mode. Once changes are completed, the Save Timesheet action persists all updates.

After saving, users can perform additional actions through the Actions menu, including:

Issue for Approval Export Timesheet Reset Timesheet

In the Issue for Approval workflow:

The user selects an approver (Supervisor, Client or Project Manager). If multiple rows are selected, then system automatically combines records and send to respective PM and Clients (records which belong to same PM or same Client will see only 1 email with multiple entries)

Upon submission, the system:

Changes the timesheet status to “Emailed”, locks timesheet row Sends an email notification to the approver User can go into View/Modify Timesheet (search timesheet) page and see timesheet row status changed to Email. Hover mouse to see whom timesheet is emailed for approval. For supervisor or PM timesheet view: Moves the record to the Pending or Pending PM queue

If the user submits the timesheet for approval without saving it first:

The system triggers an auto-save operation A confirmation prompt is displayed to avoid workflow state inconsistency

8. Approval Review & Status Updates

Supervisors and Project Managers review timesheets from their respective Pending tabs. or click on link received in email PM or Supervisor can approve / reject single timesheet at a time or bulk. For bulk approval/rejection, PM or supervisor must login to their respective Quoteplan timesheet module and navigate to Pending or Pending PM tab PM or Supervisor can write comments in the comment box to let user know reason On Approve or Reject, the system displays a confirmation popup. If timesheet is send to multiple levels of approval (supervisor AND PM and Client) then ALL of them MUST approve to change final status to Approved. If any of the approvers has rejected timesheet entry then it shows Rejected status

After confirmation:

The timesheet status is updated (either approved or rejected) The originator receives an email notification The record is removed from the pending queue Timesheet gets locked and the user can not modify the timesheet any more. (only authorized user with permission can modify Approved timesheet)

If multiple Project Managers are assigned:

Approval or rejection by one PM displays an approval indicator (tick mark). Hovering over the indicator reveals approver details.

9. Rejected Timesheet Handling

A rejected timesheet can be unlocked by the user using the locker toggle. Once unlocked, the timesheet becomes editable. The user can modify, save, and resubmit it for approval. User can not modify project however user can modify other attributes like labor, task, #of hrs, Type, Billable/non billable User can send modified timesheets for approval again. Status changes from Rejected to emailed.

Introduction

A Report is a structured presentation of data that is collected, processed, and displayed to help users understand, monitor, and analyze system information effectively.

1.Stock Reports

Stock Reports provide real-time and historical visibility of inventory across projects and categories. These reports help users track stock availability, movement, valuation, and aging, enabling effective inventory control, planning, and forecasting.

1.1. Current Stock - Overview

The Current Stock screen provides a consolidated and real-time view of inventory items available in the system. It enables users to monitor stock availability, quantities, pricing, and storage locations, supporting informed decision-making and efficient inventory management. In Quote Plan User can view Current Stock details From Current Stock Report. To View This report User needs Certain User Permission

Permission Setup Steps:

Click My Profile Go to My Settings Open User Permissions Click Edit Enable Current Stock permission Save changes In Current Stock Report Interface, details of Stock is arrange in Tabular Format User can View each stock Item along with Their Details Such as Item Id, Category, Catalog Number, Description, Make, Unit, Unit2, Minimum Quantity, Quantity in Hand(unit), Quantity in Hand(unit2), Location, Bin No, List Price, Landed Price, Stock Amount

Item ID: A unique identifier assigned to each inventory item. It is the primary reference for tracking, reporting, and system queries.

Category: Indicates the product classification.

Catalog Number: The manufacturer’s official reference or part number.

Description: Provides detailed technical and functional information about the item. Make: Identifies the manufacturer (e.g., Allen-Bradley, Schneider). Unit: Primary unit of measurement used for inventory tracking. Unit2: Secondary unit of measurement, if applicable.

Minimum Quantity: The minimum stock level required to avoid shortages.

Quantity in Hand (Unit): Actual available stock measured in the primary unit. Quantity in Hand (Unit2): Actual available stock measured in the secondary unit. Location: Physical storage location such as a warehouse or site.

Landed Price:is the per-unit cost of an item calculated by dividing the total stock amount by the quantity in hand. It represents the actual cost of each unit currently available in stock.

eg: if an item is bought at different price points and qty in hand shows item at different price points then Stock amount for that item = (purchase cost 1 * available qty 1) + (purchase cost 2 * available qty 2)….(purchase cost N * available qty N) Landed price = Stock amount of item / Total Qty in hand of that item

1.1.3 Search Functionality

The search bar at the top of the screen allows users to quickly locate current stock items. Users can search using parameters such as Item ID, Category, Catalog Number, Description, or Make, reducing the time required to find specific inventory records.

The screen provides two radio button options:

With Location - Displays current stock along with location details for each item Without Location - Displays current stock without location information This allows users to view inventory either location-wise or in a consolidated format.

1.1.5. Export Functionality

An Export button is available on the top-right corner of the screen. Users can export the displayed current stock data into file formats such as Excel or CSV for reporting, auditing, sharing with other teams, or offline analysis.

1.1.6 Filtering Functionality

Filtering options are available on columns such as Item ID, Category, Catalog Number, Description, Make, and Location. When a filter is applied, the system compares the entered value with database records and displays only the matching results. All non-matching records are temporarily hidden until the filter is cleared or modified.

Sorting can be applied to the following columns:

Item ID, Category, Catalog Number, Description, Make, Location, Unit, Quantity in Hand, Bin No, List Price Each sortable column header contains a sort icon that allows users to arrange data in ascending or descending order. Sorting only affects the display order and does not modify the underlying data.

1.1.8 Business and System Usage

The Current Stock screen supports daily inventory operations, reporting, and audit activities. It also serves as a reliable data source for automated systems, enabling accurate responses to queries related to stock avai lability, item location, pricing, and stock valuation.

1.1.9 Summary

The Current Stock screen acts as a centralized inventory monitoring tool that provides complete visibility into item availability, quantity levels, storage locations, and financial value. Its structured layout, combined with search, filtering, sorting, and export capabilities, helps users manage inventory efficiently and supports accurate operational and business decisions. A Sales Order (SO), also known as a Customer Sales Order or Customer Purchase Acknowledgement, is an internal document generated by the seller. It is created in response to a received Purchase Order (PO) from the customer. The Sales Order serves as a formal confirmation of the customer’s request and typically mirrors the details of the Purchase Order, including items, quantities, pricing, delivery terms, and milestone-based payment conditions, if applicable. Each line item in a Sales Order can be divided into payment milestones, such as Design, Build, and Deliver. Multiple milestone breakdowns are allowed for each line item to support progressive payments based on the completion of defined stages. A Sales Order (SO) is created to confirm customer requirements and define payment terms before invoicing. 1. Overview of Work Order in QuotePlan

In QuotePlan, a Work Order is an optional module used as a trigger point for manufacturing activities. Some businesses use Work Orders to initiate production after receiving a customer purchase order. Other businesses may not require Work Orders, depending on their internal processes. Work Orders are commonly used together with Sales Orders, but Sales Orders are not mandatory in QuotePlan. QuotePlan is designed to support multiple business workflows with flexibility.

2. Relationship Between Sales Order and Work Order

A Sales Order and Work Order usually go hand-in-hand, but this relationship is not compulsory.

A Work Order can be created:

With a Sales Order Without a Sales Order Directly from a Quotation Some clients do not use Sales Orders as part of their workflow. QuotePlan accommodates these variations by allowing Work Orders to be created using different reference points.

A Work Order is generally created:

After receiving a customer purchase order To trigger manufacturing or production activities Batch Production Scenario

If a customer orders a large quantity (for example, 1000 units):

It is not necessary to manufacture or ship everything at once. Production can be split into multiple batches over time using multiple Work Orders.

Typical Structure:

One Project usually has one Sales Order One Sales Order can have multiple Work Orders

A customer orders 1000 units:

Work Order 1: 200 units Work Order 2: Remaining units at a later stage This allows flexible planning and phased production.

Select a reference point:

Sales Order Project Note: Selecting a reference is mandatory to create a Work Order.

When creating a Work Order:

Only Approved Sales Orders are available for selection. Unapproved Sales Orders cannot be selected. This ensures that production does not begin without proper authorization.

Sales Orders in QuotePlan can have the following statuses:

Approved Partial Complete Cancelled Hold Under Dispatch Partial Dispatch

Statuses can also update automatically based on linked activities such as:

Material release Invoice creation Shipment creation

Once a Sales Order is approved:

Go to Create Work Order Select the approved Sales Order Drag and drop items from the Item Master Enter the required Work Order quantities

System Validation:

The system ensures that the total Work Order quantity does not exceed the Sales Order quantity This prevents accidental overproduction

Example:

Sales Order Quantity: 100 units Combined quantity of all linked Work Orders cannot exceed 100 units QuotePlan automatically enforces this balance across all related Work Orders.

The Work Order can be:

Exported as a PDF Stored for audit and record purposes Shared with shop floor or manufacturing supervisors

They act as a trigger to:

Create purchase requisitions Raise purchase orders Begin production activities

Work Orders also have their own statuses, similar to Sales Orders:

Approved Partial Cancelled Hold Dispatched

Work Order status can change automatically based on:

Invoicing Material shipment Dispatch activities

The Work Order module is tightly integrated with other QuotePlan modules, including:

Sales Orders Material Release Invoicing Shipment Quality Control

Multiple document formats such as:

Shop Order format Open Order format Acknowledgement format Quality Control format Formats can be tailored based on specific business requirements.

15. Summary

The Work Order module in QuotePlan provides a flexible and powerful way to manage manufacturing workflows.

Key Advantages:

Supports multiple business models Integrates seamlessly with other modules Prevents overproduction Offers full customization This makes it suitable for organizations with varying manufacturing and operational needs.

Q: What is introduction?
A: The Timesheet module in Quotelan is designed to record the time spent by employees on different tasks, projects, or activities. It helps organizations track labor hours, billable and non-billable hours, leave, overtime (OT), double time (DT), triple time (TT), and payroll processes. Timesheet module is also used to track punch-in/punch-out (in and out entry) of every employee to the company. Timesheets can be created, modified, approved, rejected, reset, copied, and exported based on user permissions.

By default Quoteplan shows current week Verify the selected week range and Today’s date displayed on the top-right corner. user can select 1 year prior today’s date or user can fill timesheet for 2 weeks in advance. User can fill timesheet for PTO labor code 6 months in advance. For any other labor code, system will generate message You can only create and submit PTO 6 months in advance. Select a Project from the Project dropdown. User can see only specific projects for which user is assigned. User can select only labor codes assigned for that user for that project. Also user can select assigned tasks for that project. User-labor, user-task, task-labor permissions are assigned in project module - project settings. Select a Task from the Task dropdown. (if task is enabled for your timesheet) Select Labor from the Labor dropdown. Select Type from the dropdown (REG / OT / DT / TT).

Q: What is the system automatically performs both row-level and timesheet-level calculations, including?
A: Regular Hours Overtime Double Time Triple Time Total Time (not to exceed > 24 hrs per day) Billable Hours Non-Billable Hours PTO Hours (PTO labor code) Holiday Hours (Holiday labor code) Total Hours Hours Worked (=Total hrs - non payable) Non-Payable Hours (for Lunch and FMEA labor types only) Supplemental bonus (comes from numeric value written in comment section in timesheet. Eg: $100 for customer support - this will show 100 in supplemental bonus ) All calculations are dynamically recalculated whenever hours or configuration values change.

Q: What is row management behavior?
A: After creating or opening a timesheet, users can add, edit, or delete rows. Row deletion is allowed before emailing the timesheet. After a row is deleted, all dependent calculated fields (such as Billable and Non-Billable hours) are recalculated automatically. When the Project field is changed in a row, all dependent fields (Labor, Task, Type, Hours, and Billable flag) are reset to avoid invalid data mapping. If a row contains zero hours, the system triggers a confirmation alert before saving. The Hours field accepts numeric values only

A: A Sales Order (SO), also known as a Customer Sales Order or Customer Purchase Acknowledgement, is an internal document generated by the seller. It is created in response to a received Purchase Order (PO) from the customer. The Sales Order serves as a formal confirmation of the customer’s request and typically mirrors the details of the Purchase Order, including items, quantities, pricing, delivery terms, and milestone-based payment conditions, if applicable. Each line item in a Sales Order can be divided into payment milestones, such as Design, Build, and Deliver. Multiple milestone breakdowns are allowed for each line item to support progressive payments based on the completion of defined stages. A Sales Order (SO) is created to confirm customer requirements and define payment terms before invoicing.
